Adventure log / Events, Linux Steam 53.16
Image: ELF:bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c
Source: data/runtime/native-elf-images.json reference (installed dwarfort)

This is offline binary source reconstruction. elf-decompiled.c is Ghidra C;
elf-*.asm retain the original instructions and packed/inline string operands.
elf-functions/calls/conditions/branches/switches/literals.tsv retain producer
ownership and all compiler switch edges, including aliases and empty exits.
No game process, window or translation evaluator is used by extraction.

Record construction
  17cc7c0..17cce10 owns one event card.
  If the paragraph vector is empty:
    mode 0 -> 17c06e0 incident title
    mode 1 -> 17c24d0 historical report title
    summary+68 -> complete visible title
    a separate copy is wrapped/truncated at 50 columns for indexing
    append "This event occurred on the " + ordinal day + month
           + " in the year " + signed year + "."
    mode 1 -> 17cad80 hearing/common-knowledge/mission paragraphs
  Index labels such as Attack/You and search keywords are built by 17b7d10.
  They are not complete display titles and do not license global replacements.

Incident switch at 17c0724, table 21b6354
  0 death: Your death / The death of NAME / The death of a CASTE
  1 crime: Your / NAME's / A CASTE's, then the crime noun if available
  2 attack: OWNER + " attack on " + you / NAME / a CASTE
  3 escalation: OWNER + " escalated attack on " + you / NAME / a CASTE
  4 reunion: Your reunion with NAME/somebody, or The reunion of NAME and NAME
  5 submission: OWNER + " demand of submission from " + you / NAME / a CASTE
  6 performance: 10207a0, described below
  7 artifact: ACTION + artifact name + optional recipient and location
  8 written work: placement / giving, work title or an untitled work,
                  optional recipient and location
  9 self-identification: OWNER + " self-identification to " + ENTITY
 10 refusal of identification: OWNER + " refusal to identify to " + ENTITY
  Other incident enum values append nothing.
  OWNER is Your when the native actor ID equals the adventurer's ID.
  Named actors use 12c58d0 English language_name; absent incident HF uses
  a0d5f0 RAW caste. Invalid race yields creature, not a guessed proper name.
  Identification's missing HF yields Somebody, while an empty participant
  vector appends no owner. Reunion's two absent HF branches append no name.
  These empty native fields have explicit scoped productions.

Crime switch at 17c0e4b, table 21b6380
  0 production order violation       10 crime of blood-drinking
  1 export prohibition violation      11 embezzlement
  2 job order violation               12 crime of attempted murder
  3 conspiracy to slow labor          13 crime of kidnapping
  4 crime of murder                   14 crime of attempted kidnapping
  5 disorderly conduct                15 crime of attempted theft
  6 building destruction              16 crime of treason
  7 vandalism                         17 crime of espionage
  8 crime of theft                    18 bribery
  9 crime of robbery
  A missing crime record or unsupported subtype retains the owner alone.

Artifact action selectors
  0 possession of; 1 placement of; 2 gaining of;
  3 giving of OBJECT to RECIPIENT; 4 refusal to give OBJECT to RECIPIENT;
  5 The destruction ofOBJECT (native string has no space after "of").
  Actions 0..4 can append in SITE, in REGION, in UNDERGROUND REGION, or
  in BUILDING in SITE. Native ID precedence and both building/site fields
  are retained. Written-work actions 0/1 reuse placement/giving and locations.
  a0d8c0 uses artifact language_name, Untitled for unnamed writing-bearing
  artifacts, complete item caption otherwise, or an unknown artifact.

Performance switch at 1020874, table 2125fc4
  0 telling of the story of HISTORY EVENT, with history as absent-event fallback
  1 recitation of POETIC FORM / WRITTEN WORK, with a poem fallback
  2 performance of MUSICAL FORM / COMPOSITION, with music fallback
  3 performance of DANCE FORM / WRITTEN WORK, with dance fallback
  4 sermon on HF/reference
  5 sermon on sphere
  6 sermon on the value of VALUE
  7 sermon on the worthlessness of VALUE
  Other selectors append no core; native venue handling remains independent.
  Participant lookup chooses Your or The. Musical parts choose playing if
  instrument ID exists; otherwise flags bit0 singing, bit2 chanting, speaking.
  Missing/out-of-range parts use performance. Dance role3 uses dancing;
  other dance participants use the same musical part selection.
  A known venue with a nonempty English name appends at VENUE.
  The venue-only exit also has its own scoped production; it does not assume
  a supported topic. Empty owner/victim names retain their typed event nouns.
  Existing memory-story, memory-poem, memory-performance-work and
  memory-sermon-topic scopes own all nested event/work/sphere/value fields.

Historical summary switch at 17c2514, table 21b63e0
  0 entity march, optionally toward SITE
  1 Your abduction / The abduction of HF NAME
  2 resolve original incident pointer and run 17b7d10 index initializer;
    this branch appends no additional display-title literal
  3 occupation of SITE, optionally by ENTITY
  4 Your/HF's presence, optionally in SITE or REGION
  5 ENTITY's presence, optionally in SITE
  6 ENTITY's harassment, optionally of SITE
  7 ENTITY's flight, optionally from SITE
  8 ENTITY's abandonment, optionally of SITE
  9 ENTITY's reclamation, optionally of SITE
 10 ENTITY's foundation, optionally of SITE
 11 ENTITY's march, optionally to reclaim SITE
 12 ENTITY's march, optionally to found a site in REGION
 13 ENTITY's withdrawal from, optionally followed by " of " + SITE
 14 insurrection, independently optional in SITE and against ENTITY
 15 outcome 0 overthrow of ENTITY; 1 failed insurrection against ENTITY;
    2 insurrection crushed by ENTITY; each independently optional in SITE.
    Missing entity omits its connective. Unsupported outcome retains The.
 16 Your/HF's ascension, optionally to OFFICE of ENTITY or religious SITE
 17 ENTITY's claim, optionally on SITE
 18 ENTITY's acceptance of ENTITY's offer of tribute
 19 ENTITY's refusal of ENTITY's offer of tribute
 20 ENTITY's acceptance of ENTITY's demand for tribute
 21 ENTITY's refusal of ENTITY's demand for tribute
 22 ENTITY's acceptance of ENTITY's offer of peace
 23 ENTITY's refusal of ENTITY's offer of peace
 24 ENTITY's cessation of tribute to ENTITY
 25 presence of ARTIFACT in SITE, optionally in BUILDING
 26 presence of ARTIFACT in SITE
 27 presence of ARTIFACT in SITE
 28 Your/HF's possession of ARTIFACT
 29 absence of ARTIFACT from SITE, optionally SITE's BUILDING
 30 absence of ARTIFACT from SITE
 31 absence of ARTIFACT from SITE
 32 Your/HF's lack of possession of ARTIFACT
 33 destruction of ARTIFACT
  Other selectors append nothing. Missing IDs, objects and names take their
  actual omitted-field/fallback branches; no fabricated name suffix is added.

Paragraphs at 17cad80
  You heard this / You last heard this / You first heard this
    + on the DATE + optional from INFORMANT + period
  This is common knowledge where you are from.
  You have been ordered to slay this creature.
  You have been ordered to drive these forces out.
  You have been ordered to clear the forces from this site.
  You have been ordered to cause trouble for these forces.
  Existing adventure-journal-grammar.tsv owns the six dated/informant shapes;
  ui-messages.tsv owns the five fixed paragraphs. The ordinary build imports
  all twelve months and four ordinal endings through journal-calendar-date.

Runtime integration
  adventure-journal-event-titles.tsv owns the complete incident and historical
  title grammar. Legends search and display both call translate_journal_title.
  Expanded cards retain their date/title framing. Collapsed Events cards use
  the native selected tab to retain the same title grammar without a date.
  All changes are scoped to event titles and keep complete native names.
  This source reconstruction does not claim an observed in-game result.
